```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  paste0(
    "\n\n<details>\n<summary>",
    options$summary,
    "</summary>\n\n",
    source_hook(x, options),
    "\n\n</details>\n\n"
  )
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(summary = "Show R code", message = FALSE)
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", colors = hc_theme("smpl")$colors)
```

```{r gallery-layout, include=FALSE}
gallery <- function(types, draw) {
  charts <- lapply(types, function(type) {
    draw(type) |>
      hc_title(text = type, style = list(fontSize = "16px")) |>
      hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
      hc_tooltip(outside = TRUE) |>
      hc_size(height = 235)
  })
  htmltools::div(class = "chart-grid", charts)
}
```

## Measurements and ranges

Each row is one day. Its position supplies `x`, `name` labels the day and
`y` is the mean temperature in °C. A range column extends from the day's `low`
to its `high`. With these names, `hchart(temperatures, "columnrange")` reads the
columns directly. Use `hcaes(low = minimum, high = maximum)` if your
columns have different names.

```{r temperature-data, summary="Show temperature data"}
# fmt: skip
temperatures <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name, ~y, ~low, ~high,
  "Mon", 15,   12,    18,
  "Tue", 17,   13,    21,
  "Wed", 14,   11,    17,
  "Thu", 16,   12,    20,
  "Fri", 18,   14,    22
)
```

```{r temperature-gallery, summary="Show all temperature charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "line",
    "spline",
    "area",
    "streamgraph",
    "areaspline",
    "arearange",
    "areasplinerange",
    "columnrange",
    "errorbar",
    "dumbbell",
    "polar line",
    "polar columnrange"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    hchart(
      temperatures,
      type,
      name = "Temperature",
      colorByPoint = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#2980b9",
      fillColor = "#2980b966",
      tooltip = list(valueSuffix = " °C")
    ) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        polar = startsWith(label, "polar")
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = ""), visible = type != "streamgraph")
  }
)
```

## Quantities by category

Each visit appears once, at the last shopping step it reached (`name`).
Bars, columns, cylinders and slices show how the 100 visits ended (`y`). Bars
and columns start at zero; polar columns arrange the same quantities around a
circle. A funnel counts everyone
who reached each step: 100 viewed products, 66 added to cart, 42 started checkout
and 24 purchased. For variable-width columns and variable-radius slices, `z`
is the illustrative average session duration in minutes, available for all four steps.
Variwide uses it for column width; variable pie uses it for radius, with zero
as the lower bound. The treemap subdivides the same visits by acquisition source.

```{r shopping-data, summary="Show shopping data"}
# fmt: skip
shopping <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,         ~y, ~z,
  "Viewed",      34,  2.5,
  "Added",       24,    6,
  "Checkout",    18,    9,
  "Purchased",   24,    8
)

# fmt: skip
shopping_sources <- tibble::tribble(
  ~stage,      ~source, ~value,
  "Viewed",   "Search",     18,
  "Viewed",   "Social",     10,
  "Viewed",   "Direct",      6,
  "Added",    "Search",     13,
  "Added",    "Social",      7,
  "Added",    "Direct",      4,
  "Checkout", "Search",      9,
  "Checkout", "Social",      6,
  "Checkout", "Direct",      3,
  "Purchased","Search",    12,
  "Purchased","Social",     8,
  "Purchased","Direct",     4
)
```

```{r shopping-gallery, summary="Show all shopping charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "bar",
    "column",
    "cylinder",
    "columnpyramid",
    "variwide",
    "polar column",
    "pie",
    "variablepie",
    "lollipop",
    "dotplot",
    "item",
    "waterfall",
    "packedbubble",
    "treemap",
    "wordcloud",
    "funnel",
    "pyramid",
    "funnel3d",
    "pyramid3d"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    points <- shopping
    if (type %in% c("funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d")) {
      points$y <- rev(cumsum(rev(points$y)))
    }
    if (type == "packedbubble") {
      points$value <- points$y
    }
    if (type == "treemap") {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        transmute(shopping, id = name, name),
        transmute(
          shopping_sources,
          id = paste(stage, source, sep = "-"),
          parent = stage,
          name = source,
          value
        )
      )
      return(hchart(
        nodes,
        type,
        levels = list(
          list(
            level = 1,
            colorByPoint = TRUE,
            dataLabels = list(
              enabled = TRUE,
              headers = TRUE,
              style = list(fontSize = "10px", fontWeight = "normal")
            )
          ),
          list(level = 2, colorVariation = list(key = "brightness", to = 0.2))
        ),
        dataLabels = list(enabled = FALSE),
        tooltip = list(
          pointFormat = "{point.parent} / {point.name}: {point.value} visits"
        )
      ))
    }
    if (type == "wordcloud") {
      points$weight <- points$y
    }
    hchart(points, type, name = "Visits", colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
      hc_plotOptions(
        pie = list(dataLabels = list(distance = 8)),
        variablepie = list(
          zMin = 0,
          dataLabels = list(distance = 8),
          tooltip = list(
            pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits<br>Average session: {point.z} min"
          )
        ),
        variwide = list(
          tooltip = list(
            pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits<br>Average session: {point.z} min"
          )
        ),
        packedbubble = list(zMin = 0, maxSize = "100%")
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(
        categories = points$name,
        labels = if (startsWith(label, "polar")) {
          list(distance = 5, style = list(fontSize = "10px"))
        }
      ) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        polar = startsWith(label, "polar"),
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type %in% c("cylinder", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d"),
          alpha = 12,
          beta = 15
        )
      )
  }
)
```

## Relationships and hierarchies

Each row connects a parent team (`from`) to a subteam (`to`).
The link's `weight` is the subteam's headcount. Tree and sunburst charts
express the same hierarchy with `id` and `parent`. Network nodes use
`marker.radius` to show team size.

```{r team-data, summary="Show team data"}
# fmt: skip
teams <- tibble::tribble(
  ~from,     ~to,       ~weight,
  "Studio",  "Design",       12,
  "Studio",  "Build",        18,
  "Design",  "Web",           7,
  "Design",  "Print",         5,
  "Build",   "Apps",         10,
  "Build",   "Data",          5,
  "Build",   "Tools",         3
)

team_sizes <- bind_rows(
  teams |>
    group_by(from) |>
    summarise(headcount = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") |>
    rename(id = from),
  transmute(teams, id = to, headcount = weight)
) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    marker = lapply(
      4 + 10 * sqrt(headcount / max(headcount)),
      function(radius) list(radius = radius)
    )
  )
```

```{r teams-gallery, summary="Show all team charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "sankey",
    "dependencywheel",
    "arcdiagram",
    "networkgraph",
    "organization",
    "treegraph",
    "sunburst"
  ),
  function(type) {
    if (type == "networkgraph") {
      return(hchart(
        teams,
        type,
        nodes = list_parse(team_sizes),
        layoutAlgorithm = list(enableSimulation = FALSE),
        dataLabels = list(
          enabled = TRUE,
          linkFormat = "",
          style = list(
            fontSize = "9px",
            textOutline = "none",
            fontWeight = "normal"
          )
        ),
        tooltip = list(nodeFormat = "{point.name}: {point.headcount} people")
      ))
    }
    if (type == "organization") {
      return(hchart(
        teams,
        type,
        color = "#47475c",
        colorByPoint = FALSE,
        nodeWidth = 54,
        nodePadding = 8,
        dataLabels = list(
          nodeFormat = "{point.name}",
          style = list(
            color = "#ffffff",
            fontSize = "10px",
            fontWeight = "normal",
            textOutline = "none"
          )
        )
      ))
    }
    if (type %in% c("treegraph", "sunburst")) {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        tibble(id = "Studio", name = "Studio"),
        transmute(teams, id = to, parent = from, name = to, value = weight)
      )
      if (type == "sunburst") {
        return(hchart(
          nodes,
          type,
          levels = list(list(level = 2, colorByPoint = TRUE))
        ))
      }
      return(hchart(nodes, type))
    }
    hchart(teams, type)
  }
)
```

For a network with an `igraph` layout, see the [igraph example](hchart.html#igraph-package).

## Positions, bubbles and wind

Each point is a South American capital or seat of government at its longitude
(`x`) and latitude (`y`). The rounded coordinates come from
[Natural Earth's populated places](https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/blob/master/geojson/ne_10m_populated_places_simple.geojson).
Illustrative wind speed in m/s supplies bubble size and the third dimension
(`z`), vector `length` and wind-barb `value`. `direction` gives the angle in
degrees. All points use the same color.

```{r capital-data, summary="Show capital data and illustrative winds"}
# fmt: skip
capitals <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,             ~x,     ~y, ~speed, ~direction,
  "Bogotá",      -74.09,   4.60,      6,         70,
  "Caracas",     -66.92,  10.50,      7,        100,
  "Georgetown",  -58.17,   6.80,      4,         80,
  "Paramaribo",  -55.17,   5.84,      5,         65,
  "Quito",       -78.50,  -0.21,      4,        160,
  "Lima",        -77.05, -12.05,      8,        180,
  "La Paz",      -68.15, -16.50,      6,        225,
  "Sucre",       -65.26, -19.04,      5,        250,
  "Brasília",    -47.92, -15.78,      3,         90,
  "Asunción",    -57.63, -25.29,      7,        120,
  "Santiago",    -70.65, -33.44,      5,        210,
  "Montevideo",  -56.19, -34.91,      9,        150,
  "Buenos Aires",-58.43, -34.61,     11,        135
) |> mutate(z = speed)
```

```{r capitals-gallery, summary="Show all capital charts in R"}
gallery(
  c("scatter", "bubble", "scatter3d", "vector", "windbarb", "polygon"),
  function(type) {
    points <- arrange(capitals, x)
    if (type == "polygon") {
      points <- points[chull(points$x, points$y), ]
    }
    if (type == "windbarb") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        "scatter",
        id = "cities",
        color = "#47475c",
        marker = list(radius = 2)
      ) |>
        hc_add_series(
          points,
          "windbarb",
          hcaes(value = speed),
          color = "#47475c",
          onSeries = "cities",
          yOffset = 0,
          name = "Wind"
        )
    } else if (type == "vector") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        type,
        hcaes(length = speed),
        color = "#47475c",
        vectorLength = 24,
        lineWidth = 2,
        name = "Wind"
      )
    } else {
      hc <- hchart(points, type, name = "Capitals", color = "#47475c")
    }
    hc |>
      hc_chart(
        type = if (type == "windbarb") "scatter" else type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type == "scatter3d",
          alpha = 15,
          beta = 20
        )
      ) |>
      hc_plotOptions(bubble = list(zMin = 0, minSize = 5, maxSize = "18%")) |>
      hc_xAxis(min = -82, max = -43, title = list(text = "Longitude")) |>
      hc_yAxis(min = -40, max = 15, title = list(text = "Latitude"))
  }
)
```

## Gridded measurements

Each cell has a column (`x`), a row (`y`) and a measurement (`value`).
A heatmap colors rectangular cells, a tilemap uses hexagons, and a contour joins locations with the same value.

```{r grid-data}
volcano_colors <- c("#000004", "#56106E", "#BB3754", "#F98C0A", "#FCFFA4")
cells <- expand.grid(x = 0:5, y = 0:5) |> mutate(value = sin(x) + cos(y))
```

```{r grid-types}
gallery(c("heatmap", "tilemap", "contour"), function(type) {
  hchart(cells, type) |>
    hc_colorAxis(
      min = -2,
      max = 2,
      stops = color_stops(colors = volcano_colors)
    )
})
```

## Other examples

Intervals use start and end positions. A Venn diagram sizes intersections by
`sets` and `value`, and a solid
gauge displays a single measurement (`y`).

### Comparing a measurement with a target

The bullet compares ten daily means (`y`) with a `target` of 18 °C.

```{r temperature-target}
daily <- tibble::tibble(
  name = paste(rep(c("W1", "W2"), each = 5), rep(temperatures$name, 2)),
  y = c(temperatures$y, 18, 19, 17, 20, 18)
)
hchart(
  daily,
  "bullet",
  hcaes(x = name, y = y, target = 18),
  colorByPoint = TRUE
) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Temperature (°C)")) |>
  hc_size(height = 300)
```

### Shopping timeline

A timeline places each event at its position (`x`) and labels it by `name`.
This illustrative session follows six events, with elapsed time on hover.

```{r shopping-timeline}
events <- tibble::tibble(
  name = c("Viewed", "Search", "Product", "Added", "Checkout", "Purchased"),
  x = as.POSIXct("2025-01-06 10:00:00", tz = "UTC") +
    c(0, 30, 85, 200, 310, 430)
)
hchart(
  events,
  "timeline",
  name = "Shopping steps",
  dataLabels = list(format = "{point.name}", style = list(fontSize = "11px"))
) |>
  hc_chart(type = "timeline") |>
  hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.x:%H:%M:%S}") |>
  hc_size(height = 300)
```

### Task intervals

Each row spans two dates. Map the start to `x`, the end to `x2` and the lane's zero-based index to `y`.
Here, twelve tasks share four team lanes. The three phases use different
series and colors. `grouping = FALSE` places each series on the same team lane,
while the start and finish dates determine its horizontal position.

```{r mapping-xrange}
# fmt: skip
tasks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~team,      ~phase,    ~task,        ~offset, ~days, ~progress,
  "Data",     "Prepare","Extract",         0,     3,         1,
  "Data",     "Build",  "Clean",           3,     4,         1,
  "Data",     "Review", "Validate",        7,     3,       0.8,
  "Research", "Prepare","Scope",           0,     4,         1,
  "Research", "Build",  "Analyse",         4,     5,       0.8,
  "Research", "Review", "Review",          9,     3,       0.3,
  "Design",   "Prepare","Wireframes",      1,     3,         1,
  "Design",   "Build",  "Prototype",       4,     4,       0.9,
  "Design",   "Review", "Test",            8,     4,       0.2,
  "Platform", "Prepare","Configure",       0,     2,         1,
  "Platform", "Build",  "Integrate",       5,     5,       0.5,
  "Platform", "Review", "Deploy",         11,     2,         0
) |>
  mutate(
    phase = factor(phase, levels = c("Prepare", "Build", "Review")),
    start = base::as.Date("2025-01-06") + offset,
    finish = start + days,
    lane = match(team, unique(team)) - 1L
  )
hchart(
  tasks,
  "xrange",
  hcaes(
    x = start,
    x2 = finish,
    y = lane,
    group = phase,
    name = task,
    partialFill = progress
  ),
  colorByPoint = FALSE,
  dataLabels = list(
    enabled = TRUE,
    format = "{point.name}",
    style = list(fontSize = "10px", fontWeight = "normal", textOutline = "none")
  )
) |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "")) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    categories = unique(tasks$team),
    reversed = TRUE,
    title = list(text = "")
  ) |>
  hc_plotOptions(xrange = list(grouping = FALSE, pointWidth = 22)) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    pointFormat = "{point.name}<br>{point.x:%e %b} to {point.x2:%e %b}"
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 330)
```

The same twelve intervals can be shown as Gantt tasks. Assign an ID to each
task and link the tasks within each team with `dependency`.

```{r minimal-gantt}
schedule <- tasks |>
  group_by(team) |>
  mutate(id = paste(team, row_number(), sep = "-"), dependency = lag(id)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(
    name = paste(team, task, sep = ": "),
    id,
    start = datetime_to_timestamp(start),
    end = datetime_to_timestamp(finish),
    completed = progress,
    dependency
  )
hchart(schedule, "gantt", name = "Tasks") |>
  hc_size(height = 500)
```

[See the release schedule with dependencies and completion bars](showcase.html#gantt-schedules).

### Distributions

For a histogram in R, pass the result of `hist(..., plot = FALSE)` to
`hchart()`. See the [precomputed histogram example](hchart.html#precomputed-histograms).

A box plot reads five fields per group, `low`, `q1`, `median`, `q3` and `high`.

```{r mapping-boxplot}
waits <- data.frame(
  clinic = c("North", "South", "East", "West", "Central", "Coast"),
  lower = c(4, 6, 3, 5, 7, 2),
  p25 = c(6, 8, 5, 8, 10, 5),
  p50 = c(10, 12, 9, 13, 15, 8),
  p75 = c(14, 15, 13, 17, 21, 12),
  upper = c(19, 22, 18, 24, 29, 17)
)
hchart(
  waits,
  "boxplot",
  hcaes(x = clinic, low = lower, q1 = p25, median = p50, q3 = p75, high = upper)
)
```

The `bellcurve` series fits a normal curve using the sample mean and standard
deviation. This example uses all 32 fuel-economy observations in `mtcars`.
For a kernel density estimate, see [Densities](hchart.html#densities).

```{r bellcurve}
fuel <- mtcars |> transmute(x = row_number(), y = mpg)
hchart(fuel, "scatter", id = "fuel", visible = FALSE, showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "bellcurve",
    baseSeries = "fuel",
    name = "Normal curve"
  ) |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Fuel economy (mpg)"))
```
